title: The 'bunk cave' banquets with free food and wine
summary: The banquet tradition, with free food and drink, as at Perseverance Hall; the last one played with Manuel around 1909-10.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah, we played a bunk cave. The last bunk cave we played together, Manuel. It was at the Perseverance Hall on Vero Street with George and Freddie Kemper that finished the leave. That was around 99, was it? Yeah. 99 or 1910. Around 99. I think it was nine.
See, Freddie and they were supposed to leave. Do you remember? That bunk cave. I forget what club give that thing. They had the vows of wine back there on the table.
Is that the same as the word, Creole word for banquet would you say?

Well, it was like, in other words, like a banquet they called, but they used to call it banque. Banque. See, it was like, you see, but everything was free on this thing. See, most of the banquets are now played up here. Everybody paid for their plates of food, see.
They featured the food more than the dancing? The food.

Well, you dance, you dance until that table gets ready. And they set that long table as long as that hall, that's how long the hall is, that's how long the table is going to be. And that food is on that table. And you go there, people will wear it on you. You go back with your cup to that barrel of wine and barrel of beer. Draw it. Drink. See? And there's nobody there to tell the baron to play. They'll take their intermission, go down and get something to eat. I'm going back on that stand. Back in those days, at 12 o'clock at night, you had to feed the man. The man come up. And they had the table set up for them. The table was set, that's their food they had to eat. Gumbo. Gumbo. Not the gumbo, ham and salad. Ham and salad, yeah. You see, you didn't have to ration for nothing. That was your food, you know, you had to eat. Because people back there, they believed we needed to eat. And you ate good, see? And if you didn't eat, what's the matter? You don't like what cooking? What's the matter? You don't like a bass player? What's the matter? You don't want nothing to eat? What's the matter? You don't want nothing to eat? What's wrong with it? You trying to be cute or something? Damn. Didn't tell you that man. You better go and eat. No fights. And there wasn't much to come to them dance hall and they made money. See, we had to cooperate and all. Well, before they were all the cooperators, it was the Hoops Hall, the first Hoops.
